Thanks for the context — reviewed. High-level guidance from Legal below and suggested redline language. I kept Atlas' pilot needs in mind but want to avoid a permanent carveout that undermines our standard auto-renew model.

Legal positions/recommendations:
- Pilot opt-out: we can accept a pilot-only, time-limited opt-out. Implement as an Order Form checkbox labeled "Pilot Opt-Out: Auto-Renew Disabled for Pilot Term Only" plus an explicit clause in the Order Form that the opt-out expires at the end of the pilot term unless re-signed. This preserves our ability to auto-renew for standard customers.
- Notice windows: accept 45-day notice for pilot cohorts; keep a 60-day default notice for standard enterprise renewals.
- TFC and remedies: approve cap to pro-rated refund of unused prepaid fees, plus documented offboarding costs (capped at a reasonable % or dollar amount if commercial wants stronger limits). Do not expose Redwood to broader refunds or credits without Board/legal approval. Recommend adding: "Redwood will provide up to 30 days of transitional support post-termination to assist in orderly data export and service wind-down."

Suggested sentence to add to MSA/Order Form redline: "For termination for convenience by Customer, Customer will receive a refund of any prepaid, unused fees for the remaining portion of the paid term, less reasonable offboarding expenses documented by Redwood not to exceed the greater of $25,000 or 10% of the remaining prepaid fees. Redwood will provide transitional support for a period of up to thirty (30) days to facilitate data export and service wind-down. Except for the remedies set forth in this Section, neither party shall be liable for consequential, incidental, or special damages arising from termination for convenience."

A few commercial notes: if Atlas wants the PO number route to disable auto-renew, we should ensure Order Form automation marks PO-present accounts as "manual renewal" in our billing system. Marcus — can you confirm if billing can enforce that flag?

I'll attach a clean redline (redline_attachment.docx) with the recommended language changes and a tracked-change MSA excerpt. If commercial approves the suggested cap and the pilot opt-out checkbox approach, I think we have a path to sign by end of August.

- Stephanie
